title: PRD: Tenant Fidelity Emulation and SLA Simulator
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This Product Requirements Document (PRD) describes the Tenant Fidelity Emulation and SLA Simulator (TFESS): a self-service tool and backend service used by product, SRE, sales engineering, and solution architects to model how per-tenant fidelity changes, fallback policies, and deployment-transitions (hosted -> dedicated -> private) affect latency, cost, and SLO compliance. TFESS is intended for both sandbox experimentation and deterministic pre-launch risk analysis for customer migrations and commercial packaging decisions.

Goals:
- Provide a configurable simulation engine that emits per-route and per-tenant metrics (p95 latency, token-cost, error-rate, KV-cache-hit-rate) for scenario-driven inputs.
- Model fidelity negotiation policies (requested fidelity, negotiated fallback, quantization profiles) and return projected customer-facing SLA outcomes over time windows.
- Enable "what-if" analysis for pricing and packaging teams to estimate cost delta for fidelity tiers and precompute recommended crediting adjustments for migration offers.
- Integrate with Redwood Console and Redwood Optimize to allow exporting scenario results to dashboards and to feed Optimize’s heuristics for suggested quantization profiles.

Non-goals:
- TFESS will not be a live request router nor serve production traffic.
- It does not replace the full-scale traffic runner used by performance team for kernel-level throughput benchmarking.

Background and motivation:
Redwood’s consumption model and fidelity controls (adaptive fidelity, token-budgeting, fallback variants) produce complex interactions between user prompts, KV cache behavior, batching, and quantization. Customer migration and pricing decisions frequently require multi-dimensional simulations: per-route mix, sequence length distributions, regional failover, and rollout ramp. Today these analyses are ad-hoc (spreadsheets + perf-runs) and take weeks. TFESS will standardize the simulation workflow into a repeatable, auditable toolchain.

Primary users:
- Product managers and pricing analysts (scenario creation, metric export)
- Sales engineers and solutions architects (customer migration risk reports)
- SRE and capacity planners (SLO impact and burst planning)
- Redwood Optimize team (fidelity/quantization suggestions)

Key success metrics (first 6 months):
- 80% reduction in time-to-decision for fidelity migration proposals (target: < 1 week per customer analysis).
- TFESS used in 90% of enterprise migration proposals over $50k MRR.
- Simulation-to-production delta (predicted p95 latency vs observed first-week p95) within ±15% for 75% of scenarios.

Requirements (functional):
1) Scenario definition DSL (JSON/YAML)
   - Must accept: tenant mix (list of routes + traffic weights), sequence-length histogram, per-route requested fidelity budget, geographic distribution, model variant preferences, KV-cache priming policies, and autoscaler policies.
   - Example YAML:

   scenario_name: "midmarket-migration-ny-eu"
   duration_minutes: 240
   routes:
     - id: "chat-completion"
       weight: 0.6
       seq_histogram: "short:0.5,mid:0.4,long:0.1"
       requested_fidelity: "high"
     - id: "search-embed"
       weight: 0.3
       seq_histogram: "short:0.7,mid:0.2,long:0.1"
       requested_fidelity: "standard"
     - id: "reranker"
       weight: 0.1
       seq_histogram: "short:0.2,mid:0.5,long:0.3"
       requested_fidelity: "low"

2) Engine models
   - Latency model: per-model-variant token latency distribution parameterized by seq length, batch size, and quantization profile.
   - Cost model: per-token GPU cost including amortized kernel overhead, batching efficiency, and KV cache hit/miss cost delta.
   - SLO model: map of configured SLOs (p95 latency threshold, error-rate limit) to simulated observed metrics.

3) Fidelity negotiation simulation
   - Accepts a tenant fidelity policy (priority list: requested_fidelity -> variant_fallbacks -> quantization policy) and produces per-request negotiated variant and any degradation path over the simulation window.

4) Failure and fallback injection
   - Simulate regional failover, spot/preemptible eviction, and model-variant unavailability with TTL-based recovery windows.

5) Output and export
   - Produce time-series outputs (1s/10s aggregation) for: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens produced, GPU-token-cost, error-rate, KV-cache hit-rate, batch-size distribution.
   - Exportable to: CSV, JSON, and Redwood Console import format (dashboard template).

6) API and SDK
   - HTTP API for programmatic scenario creation, execution, and result retrieval.
   - Python SDK: scenario builder, run_from_local(), fetch_results(), and download_report().

7) Auditability and traceability
   - Each run must be assigned a run_id, store scenario inputs, simulator binary/config checksum, and user who launched the run. Runs must be immutable and retained for 90 days for audit.

8) Performance and scaling
   - TFESS can run large scenarios (10k concurrent simulated tenants, 2k routes total) with runtime <= 30 minutes on a 16-GPU simulation cluster.

Acceptance criteria (with examples):
- Given a baseline scenario (hosted heavy chat traffic, p95 target 300ms), simulator predicts p95 270–330ms and after a staged rollout to dedicated with autoscaler changes, predicted p95 falls below 200ms. Validation: run validated against production pilot cluster metrics and within ±15% of observed numbers.
- SDK exposes a single-line command to reproduce a report: python -m tfess.run --scenario example.yaml --output report.json

API/SDK contract (high-level):
- POST /api/v1/scenarios -> returns scenario_id
- POST /api/v1/runs (scenario_id, runtime_config) -> returns run_id and estimated_completion_seconds
- GET /api/v1/runs/{run_id}/results -> timeseries + summary metrics
- Sample Python usage:

from tfess import Client
cli = Client(base_url="https://tfess.internal.redwood")
scenario_id = cli.create_scenario(path_to_yaml="migration.yaml")
run_id = cli.start_run(scenario_id, cluster_profile="16-gpu-fast")
results = cli.wait_and_fetch(run_id)
cli.download_report(run_id, "customer-migration-report.zip")

Telemetry and monitoring requirements:
- Instrument: scenario run state transitions, run duration, simulator memory/CPU/GPU usage, per-model simulation errors, and export failures.
- Expose Prometheus metrics for: tfess_runs_total, tfess_run_duration_seconds, tfess_simulation_errors_total, tfess_estimated_cost_usd_total.
- Circuit-breaker: abort runs that exceed 2x estimated runtime or 90% cluster utilization.

Data and privacy considerations:
- Scenarios may contain customer-sensitive example prompts or synthetic PII. All scenario input files must be stored encrypted at rest and access-controlled via RBAC.
- Default retention of scenario definitions: 90 days. Users may opt-in to longer retention for long-running engagements.

Security and compliance:
- TFESS control-plane runs in Redwood internal VPC and must authenticate via short-lived API keys tied to SSO identity.
- Audit logs forwarded to the central logging pipeline and available to Security for 365 days.

Rollout plan and milestones:
1) Alpha (Q3 2026): internal-only CLI + Python SDK, small cluster profile (4 GPUs), canonical scenario templates for migrations.
2) Beta (Q4 2026): Redwood Console integration (run creation and result preview), CSV/JSON exports, 16-GPU cluster profile.
3) GA (Q1 2027): RBAC integration, audit retention 90 days, export dashboard templates to Console, integration with Redwood Optimize for suggestions.

Dependencies and integrations:
- Redwood Console (dashboard import API)
- Redwood Optimize (API hook for feeding simulation results)
- Capacity management service (simulate autoscaler policies)
- Internal model performance table (latency/cost profiles per variant and sequence length)

Open questions (team to resolve before beta):
- Should TFESS include a stochastic request-level simulator (per-request sampling) or rely on histograms and aggregated distributions? Recommendation: implement histogram-driven engine first (deterministic) and add stochastic sampling as an opt-in later.
- Retention policy for runs longer than 90 days when used for multi-quarter customer engagements.
